prompt: Implement dedupe to return a new array with duplicate values removed, keeping only the FIRST occurrence of each value in its original order.
explanation: Because arrays are fixed-length, the trick is to collect unique values into a scratch array sized for the worst case (all distinct) while counting how many were actually kept, then shrink with Arrays.copyOf(kept, count) to the exact length. Checking only the first count slots of the scratch array is what makes 'seen before' mean 'seen among the values already kept'. A HashSet-based version also works, but the two-array approach shows what the set is doing for you.
hints: You cannot resize an array, so collect into a temp array of length a.length and track how many slots are used.
For each value, scan only the used part of the temp array to see if it was already kept.
java.util.Arrays.copyOf(kept, count) produces the exact-length final result.
